data.description:
Session recordings are written forever with no retention policy. proxy/session-recordings/ currently holds 203GB across ~13,186 session directories; there is no code anywhere that deletes or rotates recordings, and the directory is gitignored so it grows silently.

Impact: unbounded disk growth on the proxy host (critical - disk exhaustion / data loss risk).

Goal: provide an automated pruning mechanism that retains only the most recent 3 days of recordings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The proxy prunes recordings older than 3 days (delete all session-recording files with timestamps older than 3 days immediately at startup and on a periodic schedule while running).
2. Pruning must handle both the recording files and their containing session directories (remove empty session dirs after all their files are pruned).
3. Pruning must operate on the configured recording path in general (not hardcoded), including any path outside the proxy dir once LP for moving default path lands.
4. Pruning must be safe: never traverse outside the configured recording root, never follow symlinks out of the tree, guard against path traversal.
5. Pruning uses file timestamp/content timestamp rather than mtime where recordings have embedded ISO timestamps; removed content must be older than 3 days as judged from the recording filename/timestamp.
6. Prune behavior configurable in config.yaml (e.g. session_recording.retention_days, default 3; a value of 0 disables pruning).
7. All tests pass; unit tests cover: old files pruned, fresh files retained, empty dir cleanup, path-traversal safety, config-driven enable/disable.
8. Startup pruning runs in a background task and must not block proxy startup; failures logged and non-fatal.
data.title: Session recordings: no pruning mechanism; recordings accumulate unbounded (203GB, 13k sessions)
